info.bio:
Wallflowers es una banda formada en Los Ángeles (EEUU) a principios de los 90, compuesta por el vocalista y guitarrista Jakob Dylan (hijo de Bob Dylan), Fred Eltringham (batería), Rami Jaffee (teclado) y Greg Richling (bajo). Practican un rock honesto, con baladas hábiles y perspicaces y fuertes pinceladas de soul.

Jakob Dylan formó en un principio Wallflowers junto al guitarrista Tobi Miller, el teclista Rami Jaffee, el bajista Barrie Maguire y Peter Yanowitz a la cobatería.

scenes.desc: La revolución iniciada en Chicago por Souled American y Uncle Tupelo (No Depression: baladas country con la furia del hardcore) se convierte en los noventa en un género propio: sus herederos abandonan el hardcore por los sonidos más espartanos y tradicionales. Son Volt de Jay Farrar y Wilco de Jeff Tweedy (Being There, Yankee Hotel Foxtrot); Will Oldham (Palace) arranca el movimiento; Freakwater, Ida, Handsome Family, Retsin, Blue Mountain, Whiskeytown, Grant Lee Buffalo, Citizens' Utilities, Willard Grant Conspiracy. El «chamber folk» de Lambchop, Lullaby For The Working Class, Geraldine Fibbers y Pinetop Seven; el country-rock de Volebeats, Ass Ponys, Sixteen Horsepower, Old 97's y los terroristas Grifters; el folk-rock de Swell, Counting Crows, Cracker, Cake, Hootie & The Blowfish; los Black Crowes; Belle And Sebastian, Arab Strap y los polacos Atman.

podcast.title: Band Formation and Consistency
podcast.body: The Wallflowers formed from an earlier band called The Apples, morphing into their new identity by 1989 in Los Angeles. Jacob Dylan has been the sole constant member throughout the band's history, which continues to be an active concern. "And then by 1989, he was in Los Angeles with a band called The Apples, who would soon morph into The Wallflowers."

xref.title: Band Formation and Name Change
xref.body: The band was formed in Cornwall, Ontario, in 1989, originally known as The Wallflowers. They changed their name to Barstool Profits to avoid a legal conflict with Jacob Dylan's band, which also launched as The Wallflowers at almost the same time and had a major label signing. "They were formed in Cornwall, Ontario, 1989, and were originally known as the Wallflowers. But then, at almost exactly the same time, Jacob Dillon, son of Bob, launched his own band, that he called the Wallflowers. So rather than get into a fight with a major label signing, the Cornwall guy is defaulted to the bar stool profits."

xref.body: Jack Irons, a former drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Pearl Jam, was one of the musicians who cycled through the lineup of The Wallflowers. "People to cycle through the band have included former chili peppers and pro jam drummer Jack Irons."

xref.title: Guitarist Michael Ward's Subsequent Career
xref.body: Guitarist Michael Ward later became a member of The Wallflowers and joined Ben Harper's band, The Innocent Criminals. He also diversified his creative endeavors by writing children's books. "Guitarist Michael Ward eventually became a member of the Wallflowers and part of Ben Harper's band The Innocent Criminals. He also wrote some children's book."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Careers
xref.body: Following the commercial failure of their second album and subsequent breakup, the members of School of Fish pursued separate careers. One member went on to play with The Wallflowers and Ben Harper, another wrote the theme song for the TV show *Scrubs*, and singer Josh Clayton Feltz embarked on a solo career. "The band broke up with everybody going their separate ways."

xref.title: The Wallflowers' Consistency
xref.body: Jacob Dylan has been the sole consistent member of The Wallflowers throughout its existence, a band that remains active today. The lineup has seen several changes, with notable past members including Jack Irons, formerly of the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Pearl Jam, and Rami Jaffee, keyboardist for Foo Fighters. "Jacob has been the only consistent member of The Wallflowers over all these years, which by the way is still a going concern. People to cycle through the band have included former chili peppers and pro jam drummer Jack Irons and Foo Fighters keyboardist Rami Jaffee."
